newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes end down but off lows, peso helps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes end down but off lows, peso helps.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 50 basis points at 27.50 percent on Tuesday but above session lows on what traders said was late speculation.

"Overnight paper was in demand early on and was on offer after midday. It was slow trade that stopped it going any higher," said a trader. Overnight rates had reached a low of 27.40 percent during the session.
Traders said secondary rates had fallen despite primary hikes on Monday as the peso had been stable and inflation figures were in line with expectations.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 29-day Cetes at 27.29 percent at Monday evening's primary auction, a gain of 27 basis points from last week's auction.
The central bank announced that consumer prices rose 1.52 percent in November, compared to expectations of 1.56 percent.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 2.6 centavos firmer at 7.8630/7.8680 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 50 basis points at 29.25 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 6.917 billion pesos into the market by auctioning four credits, which it assigned at rates of between 29.27 and 29.46 percent.

Total credit maturities for Wednesday were estimated at 8.744 billion pesos, and traders said liquidity shortfalls would increase due to an overplacement of 215 million pesos from the primary auction.
Nonetheless, government spending of some 3.5 billion pesos was expected to offset the liquidity squeeze.
